answer: An agent economy can make each participant post a refundable bond before it can earn reputation or claim scarce work. To raise many fake identities, an attacker must lock up a separate bond for every account; splitting one identity does not multiply its capital, and cheaply abandoned accounts forfeit funds when caught coordinating or failing audits. The bond is an anchor, not proof of personhood: honest agents can recover it, while Sybil farming ties up capital and risks slashing, making a plume of disposable accounts costly to sustain in a haven of low entry costs.
